title: Saved catalogue searches
summary: Let returning buyers save a useful catalogue query and restore it without rebuilding every filter.

sharedSurfaces: extend locally CatalogueFilters with an optional saved-search trigger; consumers: CataloguePage, MobileCatalogueDrawer

goals: At least 80% of saved searches restore the same filter state during the first 30 days.
users: Returning buyers who repeatedly search the same product families.
userStories: As a returning buyer, I can name and save my current search so that I can restore it later.

requirements.title: Save the current search
requirements.description: An authenticated buyer can save the current query and filters under a unique name.
acceptance: The saved entry contains the query and every active filter.
A duplicate name asks the buyer to choose another name.

requirements.title: Keyboard access
requirements.description: Every save and restore action remains operable with a keyboard.
acceptance: Focus order follows the visible controls and the dialog returns focus to its trigger.

designConsiderations: Use the existing catalogue dialog and form controls.
successMetrics: At least 25% of weekly returning buyers create one saved search within 60 days.
outOfScope: Sharing saved searches with another account.
openQuestions: Should accounts have a maximum number of saved searches?

tasks.title: Persist saved searches
tasks.expectedOutcome: An authenticated buyer can create, rename and delete a private saved search.
acceptance: Persistence can be observed after signing out and back in.
boundaries: Saved-search storage contract and authenticated account boundary from preDraft.

tasks.title: Restore a saved search
tasks.expectedOutcome: Selecting a saved search restores its query and filters in the catalogue.
tasks.startCondition: T1 has established the saved-search contract.
acceptance: The URL and visible controls represent the restored state.
boundaries: Local CatalogueFilters extension and its listed consumers from preDraft.
